questions.text: Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) helps you move from a model that separates business and IT strategies into a model that integrates IT strategy into the overall business strategy?
questions.why: The Business Perspective helps stakeholders align their IT strategy with their business strategy, ensuring that their IT investments map directly to key business results.

questions.text: According to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF), which perspective focuses on evaluating organizational structures and roles, new skill requirements, and identifying training needs?
questions.why: The People Perspective serves as a bridge between technology and business, focusing on human resources, organizational change management, and training management.

questions.text: Which CAF perspective focuses on ensuring that skills and processes align with maximizing the business value of IT while minimizing business risks?
questions.why: The Governance Perspective provides guidance on identifying and implementing best practices for IT governance, and on supporting business processes with technology safely.

questions.text: Which CAF perspective includes principles and patterns for implementing new solutions on the cloud, and migrating on-premises workloads to the cloud?
questions.why: The Platform Perspective helps you design, implement, and optimize the architecture of AWS technology based on business goals and objectives (e.g., compute, network, storage, database provisioning).

questions.text: Which CAF perspective helps structure the selection and implementation of controls that meet the organization's compliance and risk management needs?
questions.why: The Security Perspective helps you structure the selection and implementation of security controls that meet your organization's needs, focusing on Identity and Access Management, Detective Controls, and Data Protection.

questions.text: Which CAF perspective helps you to run, use, operate, and recover IT workloads to the level that is agreed upon with your business stakeholders?
questions.why: The Operations Perspective focuses on operating and recovering IT workloads to meet the requirements of your business stakeholders. It includes service monitoring, incident management, and disaster recovery.

questions.text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, 'Perform operations as code' is a design principle of which pillar?
questions.why: Performing operations as code (defining your entire workload as code and updating it with code) is a core design principle of the Operational Excellence pillar.

questions.text: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework encompasses the ability to protect data, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies?
questions.why: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets. Key topics include confidentiality and integrity of data, identifying and managing who can do what, and protecting systems.

questions.text: The design principle 'Stop guessing capacity' is primarily associated with which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework?
questions.why: While it impacts cost, 'Stop guessing capacity' is a fundamental design principle of the Reliability pillar. Cloud elasticity allows you to scale up and down automatically, preventing resource exhaustion failures.

questions.text: Which design principle of the Well-Architected Framework encourages you to consume technologies as a service rather than asking your IT team to learn how to host and run a new technology?
questions.why: Democratizing advanced technologies (a Performance Efficiency principle) means pushing complex, advanced tech (like machine learning or NoSQL) to cloud vendors as managed services rather than managing them yourself.

questions.text: According to the Well-Architected Framework, which pillar includes the design principle 'Analyze and attribute expenditure'?
questions.why: Analyzing and attributing expenditure is a Cost Optimization design principle. It involves accurately identifying system usage and costs, and attributing IT costs to individual workload owners (e.g., using resource tagging).

questions.text: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads?
questions.why: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, including reducing energy consumption, maximizing resource utilization, and adopting more efficient hardware and software.

questions.text: Which design principle is part of the Security pillar in the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.why: Keeping people away from data is a Security design principle. It involves using mechanisms and tools to reduce or eliminate the need for direct access or manual processing of data to reduce the risk of mishandling or modification.

questions.text: Under the Reliability pillar, what is meant by the design principle 'Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability'?

options.text: Upgrade your EC2 instances to a larger instance type when demand increases.
Replace one large resource with multiple small resources to reduce the impact of a single failure.
Deploy your application in multiple cloud providers simultaneously.
Ensure that your database is always running at 100% capacity.

questions.why: Scaling horizontally (scaling out) distributes requests across multiple, smaller resources (like instances or containers). If one fails, the overall impact on the workload is minimized.

questions.text: Which design principle of the Performance Efficiency pillar emphasizes understanding how cloud services are consumed to ensure you are using the technology approach that best aligns with your workload goals?
questions.why: Mechanical sympathy means using the tool or service that best matches what you are trying to achieve (e.g., understanding the data access patterns to choose the right database engine).

questions.text: In the context of the Well-Architected Framework, what is the primary purpose of the 'AWS Well-Architected Tool'?

options.text: To automatically deploy cloud architectures based on templates.
To provide a consistent process for reviewing and measuring your cloud architectures against AWS best practices.
To monitor billing and automatically shut down expensive resources.
To act as a firewall that blocks unarchitected deployments.

questions.why: The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps you review the state of your workloads and compares them to the latest AWS architectural best practices, providing a plan on how to architect for the cloud.

questions.text: According to the Cost Optimization pillar, what is meant by 'Stop spending money on undifferentiated heavy lifting'?

options.text: Fire IT staff that perform manual tasks.
Use managed AWS services instead of managing your own infrastructure and operating systems.
Avoid using AWS support plans to save money.
Only use On-Demand instances to avoid upfront costs.

questions.why: AWS does the 'undifferentiated heavy lifting' of data center operations (racking, stacking, powering servers, patching OS). Using managed services (like RDS instead of self-hosted databases) lets you focus on your customers instead of IT infrastructure.

questions.text: Which design principle is part of the Operational Excellence pillar?
questions.why: Making frequent, small, reversible changes allows you to innovate faster while minimizing the impact of a failure. If a change causes an issue, its small scale makes it easy to identify and reverse.

questions.text: Which CAF perspective ensures you have the right incident response procedures in place?
questions.why: Incident Response is a core capability within the Security Perspective of the CAF, ensuring that your organization has the architecture and processes to respond to security incidents.

questions.text: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework includes the design principle 'Anticipate failure'?
questions.why: While 'automatically recover from failure' is Reliability, 'Anticipate failure' (identifying potential sources of failure so they can be removed or mitigated, and testing failure scenarios) is a design principle of Operational Excellence.

questions.text: A bank must keep customer data inside its own data center because of a regulation, but wants to run it on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS using the same AWS APIs and tools it uses in the cloud. Which option fits?
questions.why: AWS Outposts puts AWS-managed racks or servers inside YOUR building, so data stays on your premises while you use the same AWS services, APIs, and console. Local Zones and Regions are AWS-owned facilities, so the data would leave your data center.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A game studio has no data center of its own. Its players are in Los Angeles and need single-digit millisecond latency, but the closest AWS Region is hundreds of miles away. What should the studio use?

options.text: An additional Availability Zone in the same Region

questions.why: AWS Local Zones place AWS compute, storage, and database services in large cities like Los Angeles, close to end users, so latency-sensitive apps like real-time gaming get single-digit millisecond latency. Outposts would need a building of your own to install it in; edge locations only cache content for CloudFront and don't run your game servers.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: Who owns and operates the building where AWS Local Zones infrastructure runs?

options.text: A colocation partner chosen by the customer

questions.why: Local Zones are AWS facilities: AWS owns and runs the building and the hardware, just like a Region, only placed in a big city closer to users. That's the key difference from Outposts, where the hardware sits in the customer's own data center. (Inside a telecom carrier's 5G network is Wavelength Zones.)
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for the physical security, power, and network connection of the site where an AWS Outposts rack is installed?

options.text: The AWS Partner that sold the rack

questions.why: Because Outposts lives in the customer's own building, the customer handles the site: physical security and access, power, cooling, and the network uplink. AWS still owns, monitors, maintains, and replaces the Outposts hardware and the AWS services running on it.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the difference between AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts?

options.text: Local Zones are installed in your data center; Outposts are AWS buildings in large cities.
Local Zones are AWS-run infrastructure in large metro areas near users; Outposts are AWS-managed hardware installed in your own data center or on-premises site.
Both run inside telecom 5G networks, but Outposts are faster.
Local Zones are for storage only; Outposts are for compute only.

questions.why: Remember it as: Local Zones = AWS comes to your CITY (AWS's building, near your users). Outposts = AWS comes to your BUILDING (AWS hardware on your premises). Both run AWS services such as EC2 and EBS with the same APIs.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A manufacturer needs to process data from factory machines with very low latency to equipment on its plant floor, using AWS services, without sending the data to an AWS Region first. Which option is the best fit?
questions.why: When the low latency you need is to systems inside your own facility (factory equipment, on-prem databases, local medical devices), Outposts is the answer: the AWS hardware sits right next to them. Local Zones lower latency to users in a city, not to machines inside your building.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A visual effects company in a major city wants to rent extra rendering capacity close to its artists for a few months, paying only for what it uses and without buying or housing any hardware. Which option fits?

options.text: Dedicated Hosts in a distant Region

questions.why: Local Zones offer pay-as-you-go AWS capacity in large metro areas, with nothing to install or house, which suits short-term, latency-sensitive work like media rendering. Outposts means hardware delivered to and kept in your own site on a 3-year term.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: How is AWS Outposts purchased?

options.text: Per second On-Demand with no commitment, like EC2
As a 3-year term, with all upfront, partial upfront, or no upfront payment options
By bidding on spare capacity, like Spot Instances
It is free with any AWS Support plan

questions.why: Outposts racks and servers are ordered for a 3-year term (all upfront, partial upfront, or no upfront). That commitment fits because AWS ships and installs physical hardware at your site. Local Zones, by contrast, are pay-as-you-go like a normal Region.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A mobile app running on 5G phones needs ultra-low latency, so its back end should run inside the telecom carrier's 5G network. Which AWS option is designed for this?
questions.why: Wavelength Zones put AWS compute and storage inside telecom providers' 5G networks, so traffic from mobile devices doesn't have to leave the carrier network. Think: Wavelength = 5G carrier, Local Zones = city, Outposts = your building.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: Which statement about AWS Outposts is true?

options.text: It runs completely disconnected from AWS with no need for a Region.
AWS installs it in an AWS-owned building near your city.
It is an extension of an AWS Region and needs a reliable network connection back to that Region.
The customer is responsible for replacing failed Outposts hardware.

questions.why: Each Outpost is tied to a parent AWS Region and is managed through a connection back to it (the console, APIs, and control plane live in the Region). AWS replaces failed hardware. An AWS-owned building near your city describes Local Zones.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: What do AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts have in common?

options.text: Both are installed inside the customer's data center.
Both extend an AWS Region, letting you run AWS services like EC2 and EBS with the same APIs, tools, and console.
Both are only for caching static website content.
Both require AWS Direct Connect and cannot use the internet.

questions.why: Both are extensions of a parent AWS Region: you use the same AWS APIs, tools, and console to run services such as EC2, EBS, and ECS closer to where you need them. The difference is location: Local Zones are AWS facilities in a city, while Outposts are in your own building.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A company must keep its data inside a country where there is no AWS Region. It already runs its own data center in that country. Which AWS option lets it use AWS services while meeting this data residency requirement?

options.text: An AWS Region in a neighboring country

questions.why: Outposts can be installed in your own data center wherever you operate, so data stays in the country while you use AWS services. A Local Zone only helps if AWS has built one in that location, and a neighboring country's Region would move the data across the border.
questions.source: Practice Questions Local Zones vs Outposts

questions.text: A company wants to grant a 3rd party application access to their AWS account without sharing long-term credentials. Which service or feature should they use?
questions.why: AWS STS enables the creation of temporary, limited-privilege credentials to access AWS resources, which is ideal for cross-account or 3rd party access without sharing permanent access keys.

questions.text: An application runs batch jobs that can be interrupted and resumed without issues. The jobs take several hours to complete. Which EC2 purchasing option provides the most cost-effective solution?
questions.why: Spot Instances can offer up to a 90% discount compared to On-Demand pricing. They are the most cost-efficient option for workloads that are resilient to failure and can be interrupted, such as batch processing.

questions.text: A company needs to store regulatory documents for 7 years. The documents are rarely accessed, but when they are needed for compliance audits, they must be retrieved within milliseconds. Which S3 storage class is most appropriate?
questions.why: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval offers millisecond retrieval for long-term storage of data accessed maybe once a quarter, making it cheaper than Standard-IA but faster than Flexible Retrieval.

questions.text: A gaming company needs a fully managed, in-memory data store with sub-millisecond latency to maintain a real-time multiplayer leaderboard. Which AWS service fits this requirement?
questions.why: ElastiCache is a managed Redis or Memcached in-memory database that provides high performance and sub-millisecond latency, perfect for read-intensive caching workloads like leaderboards.

questions.text: You are designing a microservices architecture and want to run a Docker container without provisioning or managing any underlying EC2 instances. Which compute option should you choose?

options.text: Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type

questions.why: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers. It allows you to run Docker containers on ECS or EKS without having to manage the underlying EC2 infrastructure.

questions.text: A development team wants to deploy their application code and infrastructure together using familiar programming languages like Python and TypeScript instead of writing JSON/YAML templates. Which AWS tool allows this?
questions.why: AWS CDK allows developers to define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages (like Python, Java, JS/TS). The code is then compiled down into CloudFormation templates.

questions.text: An application is deployed in multiple AWS regions. You need to route users to the region that provides the fastest response time for them. Which Route 53 routing policy should you use?
questions.why: Latency Routing Policy is specifically designed to route user traffic to the AWS region that provides the lowest network latency, optimizing the global user experience.

questions.text: A media processing pipeline uses multiple microservices. You need to decouple the video upload service from the encoding service to handle sudden spikes in traffic without losing requests. Which service should you use?
questions.why: SQS is a message queue service used to decouple application tiers. If traffic spikes, messages wait safely in the queue until the encoding consumer service can process them.

questions.text: You need to track and audit all API calls made within your AWS account to identify which IAM user deleted a specific critical S3 bucket. Which service provides this capability?
questions.why: AWS CloudTrail provides governance, compliance, and auditing by recording a history of events and API calls made within the AWS account via the Console, SDK, or CLI.

questions.text: Your EC2 instances in a private subnet need to download software updates from the internet, but they must not be reachable from the internet. What VPC component is required to enable this?
questions.why: A NAT Gateway (placed in a public subnet) allows instances in private subnets to initiate outbound IPv4 traffic to the internet while preventing inbound traffic initiated from the internet.

questions.text: A security team wants to automatically detect and alert on sensitive information, such as personally identifiable information (PII), stored in their Amazon S3 buckets. Which service should they enable?
questions.why: Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching specifically to discover and protect sensitive data (like PII) in Amazon S3.

questions.text: A customer service center wants to build a conversational chatbot that uses Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Natural Language Understanding (NLU). Which AWS Machine Learning service should they use?
questions.why: Amazon Lex is the service used to build conversational bots (chatbots). It uses the same ASR and NLU technology that powers Alexa to recognize intent from text and speech.

questions.text: A large enterprise wants to enforce compliance by explicitly preventing developers in specific AWS accounts from launching Amazon EMR clusters, regardless of their IAM permissions. How can this be centrally enforced?

options.text: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations

questions.why: SCPs are used within AWS Organizations to restrict account privileges. They apply to all users (including the root user) and can explicitly blacklist or whitelist AWS services for entire accounts or OUs.

questions.text: A company needs a scalable network file system that can be mounted concurrently by hundreds of Linux EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Which storage service should they choose?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.why: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a managed network file system (NFS) that can be mounted by hundreds of Linux EC2 instances simultaneously across multiple Availability Zones.

questions.text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which of the following is a design principle that falls under the Reliability pillar?
questions.why: Testing recovery procedures is a core design principle of the Reliability pillar. It encourages using automation to simulate different failures to ensure the system can recover seamlessly.

questions.text: A company wants to stop guessing capacity and automatically scale their web servers based on the actual load. Which cloud computing characteristic does this represent?
questions.why: Rapid elasticity and scalability allow you to automatically and quickly acquire and dispose of resources when needed, scaling out and in based on actual demand.

questions.text: Which AWS deployment model keeps some servers on-premises while extending some capabilities into the AWS Cloud?
questions.why: A Hybrid Cloud deployment model combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources, allowing control over sensitive assets while leveraging cloud flexibility.
questions.concept: Private vs Public vs Hybrid Cloud

questions.text: A company is migrating a legacy application that requires a specific, complicated per-socket software license. Which EC2 purchasing option allows them to bring this license to AWS?
questions.why: Dedicated Hosts provide a physical server with EC2 capacity fully dedicated to your use, giving you visibility into sockets and cores, which is required for Bring Your Own License (BYOL) scenarios.

questions.text: Which EC2 instance type family is best suited for in-memory databases and distributed web scale cache stores?
questions.why: Memory Optimized instances deliver fast performance for workloads that process large datasets in memory, such as high-performance relational or in-memory databases.

questions.text: If an EC2 instance in a private subnet needs to access the internet to download patches without allowing inbound traffic from the internet, what must be configured?
questions.why: A NAT Gateway (or NAT Instance) placed in a public subnet allows instances in private subnets to connect to the internet while preventing the internet from initiating connections to those instances.

questions.text: Which VPC feature acts as a stateless firewall at the subnet level, where you must explicitly define both ALLOW and DENY rules?
questions.why: Network ACLs act as a stateless firewall for subnets. Because they are stateless, return traffic must be explicitly allowed, and you can create both ALLOW and DENY rules.

questions.text: Which service provides a highly available, scalable, fully managed file system that can be mounted by hundreds of Linux EC2 instances simultaneously?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.why: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a managed network file system (NFS) that scales automatically and can be attached to hundreds of Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs.

questions.text: A business wants to store database backups for 6 months. The data is rarely accessed but must be available immediately if a disaster occurs. Which S3 storage class is the most cost-effective choice?
questions.why: S3 Standard-IA is cost-optimized for data that is infrequently accessed but requires rapid, millisecond access when needed (unlike standard Glacier, which has retrieval delays).

questions.text: Which database service provides a fully managed, serverless, key-value NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale?
questions.why: DynamoDB is AWS's fully managed, highly available, key-value NoSQL database designed for massive scale and single-digit millisecond latency.

questions.text: A data analytics team wants to query data stored directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL without provisioning any infrastructure. Which service should they use?
questions.why: Amazon Athena is an interactive, serverless query service that allows you to easily analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL.

questions.text: An application consists of tightly coupled microservices. You want to decouple these services by introducing a highly scalable, fully managed message queue. Which service fits this requirement?
questions.why: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service used to decouple application components and process messages asynchronously.

questions.text: Which AWS service allows you to distribute incoming HTTP and HTTPS web traffic across multiple targets (like EC2 instances) in multiple Availability Zones?
questions.why: The Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and routes traffic to targets within Amazon VPC based on the content of the request.

questions.text: You want to automate the creation of your AWS infrastructure using code written in JSON or YAML. Which service provides this Infrastructure as Code (IaC) capability?
questions.why: AWS CloudFormation allows you to define and provision AWS infrastructure predictably and repeatedly using declarative JSON or YAML templates.

questions.text: Which AWS security service uses Machine Learning to continuously analyze VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, and CloudTrail Events to detect malicious or unauthorized behavior?
questions.why: Amazon GuardDuty is an intelligent threat discovery service that uses machine learning and anomaly detection on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to protect your AWS account.

questions.text: A developer needs to store and automatically rotate database credentials and API keys securely. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Secrets Manager is specifically designed to store, retrieve, and automatically rotate database credentials, API keys, and other secrets.

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is the customer's responsibility?

options.text: Physical security of the data center
Patching the Amazon RDS operating system
Configuring AWS WAF rules and EC2 security groups

questions.why: Customers are responsible for 'Security IN the Cloud', which includes configuring firewalls (Security Groups, WAF), managing IAM, and encrypting customer data.

questions.text: A company requires a private, dedicated physical connection between their on-premises data center and AWS that does not travel over the public internet. What service provides this?
questions.why: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private network connection from your premises to AWS, bypassing the public internet for increased security and consistent network performance.

questions.text: Which AWS machine learning service provides highly accurate, real-time personalized product recommendations based on user history, similar to Amazon.com?
questions.why: Amazon Personalize is a fully managed ML service that allows developers to easily build applications with real-time personalized recommendations.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: An organization wants to centrally manage billing and apply compliance policies (SCPs) across multiple AWS accounts. Which service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Organizations allows you to consolidate billing across multiple accounts and apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) to centrally manage permissions and compliance.

questions.text: Which tool provides automated recommendations to optimize costs, improve performance, increase security, and monitor service quotas based on AWS best practices?
questions.why: AWS Trusted Advisor acts as an automated cloud expert, analyzing your account to provide recommendations across Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits.

questions.text: A company is migrating an application 'as-is' from their on-premises data center to AWS EC2 instances without making any architectural changes. Which migration strategy (7Rs) does this represent?
questions.why: Rehosting, also known as 'lift-and-shift', involves migrating applications to AWS without making any changes to the underlying architecture.

questions.text: Which AWS service should be used to protect a web application running on an ALB against common Layer 7 web exploits like SQL injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?
questions.why: AWS Web Application Firewall (WAF) helps protect web applications against common web exploits at Layer 7 by letting you define rules that filter HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

questions.text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, 'democratizing advanced technologies' and 'using serverless architectures' are design principles for which pillar?
questions.why: Performance Efficiency focuses on using IT and computing resources efficiently. Democratizing advanced technologies (using managed services) and adopting serverless are key principles here.

questions.text: A company needs to analyze trillions of events per day from IoT devices and requires a fast, serverless time-series database. Which AWS service fits this need?
questions.why: Amazon Timestream is a fast, scalable, serverless time-series database optimized for IoT and operational applications to store and analyze trillions of events daily.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: Which AWS service allows developers to quickly build, test, and deploy applications without worrying about infrastructure management, acting as a Platform as a Service (PaaS)?
questions.why: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) that handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and application health monitoring automatically so developers can just deploy code.

questions.text: Which AWS global infrastructure component is used to cache content closer to end-users to reduce latency?
questions.why: Edge Locations are endpoints for AWS CloudFront (the CDN service) used to cache content closer to users globally, reducing latency.

questions.text: Which AWS Support plan provides access to a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
questions.why: Only the Enterprise Support plan provides access to a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) to provide proactive guidance and best practices.

questions.text: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of running a specific architecture on AWS before actually provisioning any resources. Which tool should they use?
questions.why: The AWS Pricing Calculator allows you to estimate the cost of AWS services and architectural solutions before you build them.

questions.text: A developer needs to execute a backend script in response to an image being uploaded to an S3 bucket. The script takes 3 seconds to run. Which compute service is the most cost-effective?
questions.why: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events (like an S3 upload). You only pay for the exact compute time used (e.g., 3 seconds).

questions.text: Which storage option provides temporary, block-level storage physically attached to the host computer of an EC2 instance, where data is lost if the instance is stopped?
questions.why: EC2 Instance Store provides temporary (ephemeral) block storage that is physically attached to the host. If the instance stops or terminates, the data is permanently lost.

questions.text: A company needs to transport 80 Terabytes of data from their on-premises data center to AWS. Their internet connection is slow and it would take months to transfer. Which service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Snowball Edge is a physical data transport device used to move petabyte-scale data into and out of AWS securely and quickly when internet connections are insufficient.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: Which AWS service is used to create and manage cryptographic keys that secure your data across various AWS services?
questions.why: AWS KMS is a managed service that makes it easy to create and manage cryptographic keys and control their use across a wide range of AWS services.

questions.text: A security auditor needs to download AWS compliance reports, such as SOC and PCI-DSS certificates, to prove that the AWS infrastructure is compliant. Where can they find these?
questions.why: AWS Artifact is your go-to, central resource for compliance-related information. It provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports.

questions.text: You need to run a relational database on AWS and want to ensure it remains available even if an entire Availability Zone goes down. What feature should you enable?
questions.why: RDS Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability and failover support by automatically provisioning and maintaining a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone.

questions.text: Which AWS service provides user sign-up, sign-in, and access control for web and mobile applications?
questions.why: Amazon Cognito lets you add user sign-up, sign-in, and access control to your web and mobile apps quickly and easily (often providing federated access via Google, Facebook, etc.).

questions.text: An application needs to publish alert messages to multiple subscriber systems simultaneously, including sending emails to administrators. Which service allows this Pub/Sub messaging?
questions.why: Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) is a highly available, durable, secure, fully managed pub/sub messaging service that enables you to decouple microservices and send emails/SMS.

questions.text: A company wants to simplify their network architecture by connecting thousands of VPCs and their on-premises networks using a single central hub. Which service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central cloud router (hub and spoke model) to connect your Amazon VPCs, on-premises data centers, and SD-WAN gateways.

questions.text: Which AWS service is specifically designed to analyze images and videos to detect objects, people, text, scenes, and activities?
questions.why: Amazon Rekognition makes it easy to add image and video analysis to your applications using proven, highly scalable deep learning technology.

questions.text: You want to automate the patching of operating systems across a fleet of 500 Amazon EC2 instances to ensure they meet security baselines. Which service helps achieve this?
questions.why: AWS Systems Manager (specifically Patch Manager) automates the process of patching managed instances with both security related and other types of updates.

questions.text: Which service tracks changes to the configuration of your AWS resources over time, allowing you to audit compliance and troubleshoot issues?
questions.why: AWS Config enables you to assess, audit, and evaluate the configurations of your AWS resources, keeping a historical record of configuration changes.

questions.text: A company is experiencing large DDoS attacks on their web application and wants advanced protection that includes financial protection against scaling charges caused by the attack. Which service should they subscribe to?
questions.why: AWS Shield Advanced provides expanded DDoS attack protection for web applications, access to the 24x7 DDoS Response Team (DRT), and cost protection against resource scaling spikes.

questions.text: A developer is building a microservices architecture and needs a tool to visually trace requests as they travel through the various services to identify performance bottlenecks. What tool should they use?
questions.why: AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug distributed applications, such as those built using a microservices architecture, by tracing user requests.

questions.text: You want to define permissions in a JSON document and attach it to an IAM user to restrict what AWS services they can access. What is this JSON document called?
questions.why: An IAM Policy is a JSON document that defines the specific permissions (Allow/Deny actions on resources) which can be attached to IAM users, groups, or roles.

questions.text: Which service allows you to write, run, and debug code with just a browser, acting as a cloud-based Integrated Development Environment (IDE)?
questions.why: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based integrated development environment (IDE) that lets you write, run, and debug your code with just a browser.
questions.priorityNote: closed to new customers, not on the in-scope list

questions.text: A gaming application has a global audience. The company wants to route users to the AWS Region that is geographically closest to them. Which Route 53 routing policy should they use?
questions.why: Geolocation routing lets you choose the resources that serve your traffic based on the geographic location of your users (e.g., routing all European users to the Frankfurt region).

questions.text: Which database service is a fully managed MongoDB-compatible document database?
questions.why: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fast, scalable, highly available, and fully managed document database service that supports MongoDB workloads.

questions.text: A startup wants to quickly launch a simple WordPress website on a virtual private server with a fixed monthly price. Which service is best suited for this?
questions.why: Amazon Lightsail provides easy-to-use virtual private servers (VPS) with everything needed to jumpstart a project (like WordPress) at a predictable, low monthly price.

questions.text: You want to receive an email notification when your AWS bill is projected to exceed $1,000 this month. Which tool should you configure?
questions.why: AWS Budgets allows you to set custom cost and usage budgets and receive alerts (via email or SNS) when your costs exceed (or are forecasted to exceed) your budgeted amount.

questions.text: Which fully managed big data service makes it easy to run Apache Hadoop, Spark, and Presto frameworks to process vast amounts of data?
questions.why: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce) is a cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open source tools such as Apache Spark, Apache Hive, Apache HBase, Apache Flink, Apache Hudi, and Presto.

questions.text: Which service acts as a serverless event bus that connects application data from your own apps, SaaS, and AWS services, allowing you to route events to targets?
questions.why: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that makes it easy to connect applications together using data from your own applications, integrated SaaS applications, and AWS services.

questions.text: A company wants to run some of their AWS infrastructure on-premises within their own physical data center to meet ultra-low latency requirements. Which service provides this capability?
questions.why: AWS Outposts brings native AWS services, infrastructure, and operating models to virtually any data center, co-location space, or on-premises facility.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of deploying an Amazon RDS database with Read Replicas?
questions.why: Read Replicas allow you to scale out beyond the capacity constraints of a single DB instance for read-heavy database workloads by routing read queries to the replicas.

questions.text: You want to automate your software release process by creating a CI/CD workflow that builds, tests, and deploys your code every time there is a code change. Which service orchestrates this?
questions.why: AWS CodePipeline is a fully managed continuous delivery service (CI/CD orchestration) that helps you automate your release pipelines for fast and reliable application updates.

questions.text: How does AWS Global Accelerator improve the performance of your global applications?

options.text: By caching static content at Edge Locations
By routing traffic over the AWS global network infrastructure using static IP addresses
By automatically increasing the CPU of your EC2 instances
By compressing images before sending them to users

questions.why: AWS Global Accelerator uses the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network to route user traffic, providing two static Anycast IP addresses and improving latency and throughput.

questions.text: An application needs to continuously capture and stream massive volumes of clickstream data from a website to an Amazon S3 bucket in real-time. Which service is designed for this?
questions.why: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is the easiest way to reliably load streaming data into data lakes, data stores (like S3 or Redshift), and analytics services in near real-time.

questions.text: Which component allows an EC2 instance to assume temporary credentials securely instead of hardcoding access keys in the application source code?
questions.why: An IAM Role is an identity with permission policies that determine what the identity can and cannot do. EC2 instances can assume a role to obtain temporary credentials to securely access AWS services.

questions.text: Which database service allows you to migrate an existing on-premises PostgreSQL database to AWS with minimal downtime?
questions.why: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) helps you migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely. The source database remains fully operational during the migration, minimizing downtime.

questions.text: Which AWS pricing model allows customers with predictable workloads to commit to a 1- or 3-year term in exchange for significant discounts compared to On-Demand pricing?
questions.why: Savings Plans (and Reserved Instances) offer lower prices than On-Demand pricing in exchange for a commitment to a specific amount of usage for a 1- or 3-year period.

questions.text: Which AWS networking service allows you to create a secure, private connection between your on-premises network and your Amazon VPC over the public internet?
questions.why: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates a secure IPsec VPN connection between your corporate data center and your AWS VPC, encrypting traffic over the public internet.

questions.text: A developer needs to store unstructured data consisting of millions of high-resolution images. The storage must be highly durable and infinitely scalable. Which service is the best fit?
questions.why: Amazon S3 is an object storage service designed for storing and retrieving any amount of unstructured data (like images, videos, backups) with 99.999999999% (11 9s) of durability.

questions.text: Which AWS service enables you to build visual workflows to coordinate and orchestrate multiple AWS Lambda functions?
questions.why: AWS Step Functions is a serverless function orchestrator that makes it easy to sequence AWS Lambda functions and multiple AWS services into business-critical applications (using visual workflows).

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is the responsibility of AWS?

options.text: Encrypting data at rest in Amazon S3
Physical security of AWS data centers
Patching the guest operating system on EC2 instances

questions.why: AWS is responsible for 'Security OF the Cloud,' which includes protecting the physical infrastructure, facilities, hardware, and the global network.

questions.text: Which service should you use to monitor the CPU utilization of your EC2 instances and trigger an alarm if it goes above 80%?
questions.why: Amazon CloudWatch collects monitoring and operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events. It can trigger alarms (like scaling actions or SNS notifications) based on thresholds like CPU utilization.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that all newly created S3 buckets automatically have versioning and logging enabled. Which service allows them to define these rules and automatically check compliance?
questions.why: AWS Config rules allow you to define desired configurations (like enforcing S3 versioning) and continually evaluate your resources against those rules for compliance.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used as a managed graph database designed for highly connected datasets, like social networking feeds or fraud detection?
questions.why: Amazon Neptune is a fast, reliable, fully managed graph database service built for storing and navigating highly connected relationships (using property graphs or RDF).

questions.text: Which AWS service provides a personalized view into the performance and availability of the AWS services underlying your specific AWS resources?

options.text: AWS Health Dashboard – Your account health

questions.why: The AWS Health Dashboard's Your account health view (formerly the Personal Health Dashboard) shows events that affect your own AWS resources, with alerts and remediation guidance. The Service health view (formerly the Service Health Dashboard) shows the general status of every AWS service.

questions.text: What is the most cost-effective EC2 pricing option for a workload that cannot be interrupted and will run continuously for exactly 3 months?
questions.why: Because the workload runs for only 3 months, On-Demand is the most cost-effective. Reserved Instances require a minimum 1-year commitment, and Spot Instances can be interrupted.

questions.text: Which AWS security service specifically helps protect your applications against SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks?
questions.why: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) helps protect web applications or APIs against common web exploits and bots, such as SQL injection and XSS, that may affect availability or compromise security.

questions.text: A company wants to transfer 100 Petabytes of data to AWS. Which data transfer service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data transfer service used to move extremely large amounts of data (up to 100 PB per Snowmobile) to AWS via a 45-foot long ruggedized shipping container.
questions.priorityNote: retired by AWS

questions.text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a design principle of which pillar?
questions.why: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while delivering business value. Enforcing strong identity foundations (like MFA) is a core principle.

questions.text: Which of the following acts as an automated security assessment service that helps improve the security and compliance of applications deployed on AWS by checking for unintended network accessibility and vulnerabilities?
questions.why: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continually scans AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

questions.text: Which AWS service enables you to securely connect a large number of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub?
questions.why: AWS Transit Gateway connects VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub. This simplifies your network and puts an end to complex peering relationships.

questions.text: A developer needs a service to host a highly scalable, serverless graph database. Which AWS service is appropriate?
questions.why: Amazon Neptune is a fast, reliable, fully managed graph database service built for storing and navigating highly connected datasets.

questions.text: Which AWS support plan provides a guaranteed response time of under 15 minutes for business-critical system down events?
questions.why: Only the Enterprise Support plan provides a 15-minute response time SLA for business-critical system down events. Business support is 1 hour.

questions.text: What does Amazon CloudFront use to deliver content with low latency to users globally?
questions.why: CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) that caches data, videos, APIs, and applications at Edge Locations globally to reduce latency for end-users.

questions.text: You want to automate the provisioning of your AWS infrastructure using declarative templates written in JSON or YAML. Which service allows this?
questions.why: AWS CloudFormation is the Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service that lets you model, provision, and manage AWS resources using JSON/YAML templates.

questions.text: Which AWS service is best suited to run Docker containers in a fully managed, serverless environment without managing underlying EC2 instances?
questions.why: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with Amazon ECS and EKS, removing the need to provision or manage servers.

questions.text: A company wants to host an enterprise data warehouse to analyze petabytes of complex relational data. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.why: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse service specifically designed for running complex analytical queries on massive datasets.

questions.text: Which tool provides recommendations for optimizing AWS resources, improving security, saving money, and closing compliance gaps?
questions.why: AWS Trusted Advisor acts as a customized cloud expert, evaluating your account by providing checks across Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits.

questions.text: A company wants to convert their text-based blog posts into lifelike speech audio files. Which AWS Machine Learning service should they use?
questions.why: Amazon Polly is an ML service that turns text into lifelike speech, allowing you to create applications that talk and build entirely new categories of speech-enabled products.

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which task is the sole responsibility of AWS?
questions.why: AWS is responsible for 'Security OF the Cloud,' which inherently includes the physical security of data centers, hardware, and underlying network infrastructure.

questions.text: Which AWS pricing model gives you the ability to bid on spare Amazon EC2 computing capacity at a significant discount?
questions.why: Spot Instances allow you to request unused EC2 capacity at steep discounts (up to 90%), but they can be interrupted if AWS needs the capacity back.

questions.text: Which service acts as an omnichannel cloud contact center that can be set up quickly to improve customer service operations?
questions.why: Amazon Connect is a highly scalable, easy-to-use, cloud-based contact center service (call center) that helps businesses provide superior customer service at a lower cost.

questions.text: A developer needs to store application session state with sub-millisecond response times. Which in-memory database service is the best fit?
questions.why: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) is a fully managed in-memory data store providing sub-millisecond latency, making it ideal for caching and session management.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of deploying an application across multiple Availability Zones?
questions.why: Deploying across multiple AZs ensures that if a single data center (AZ) fails, the application remains available, providing High Availability and Fault Tolerance.

questions.text: Which service allows a company to logically isolate its AWS resources in a private virtual network?
questions.why: Amazon VPC lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a virtual network that you define.

questions.text: A company wants to identify and organize their AWS resources by attaching metadata such as 'Environment: Production' or 'Project: Alpha'. What feature should they use?
questions.why: Tags are key-value pairs assigned to AWS resources that help manage, identify, organize, search for, and filter resources, as well as allocate costs.

questions.text: Which AWS database service provides a MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database that is up to 5 times faster than standard MySQL databases?
questions.why: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL that offers high performance, scaling, and up to 5x the throughput of standard MySQL.

questions.text: A developer wants to upload a script, and have AWS automatically handle the provisioning, load balancing, and auto-scaling of the environment. Which service acts as a Platform as a Service (PaaS)?
questions.why: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an easy-to-use PaaS for deploying and scaling web applications and services. You simply upload your code, and it handles the deployment and provisioning.

questions.text: An organization wants to centrally manage multiple AWS accounts, consolidate billing, and apply hierarchical security policies. Which service should they use?
questions.why: AWS Organizations provides central governance and management across multiple AWS accounts, allowing for consolidated billing and the application of Service Control Policies (SCPs).

questions.text: Which storage service provides highly durable, block-level storage volumes that can be attached to Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.why: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) provides highly available, consistent, low-latency block storage volumes for use with Amazon EC2 instances.

questions.text: Which AWS networking service connects a VPC directly to supported AWS services (like S3 or DynamoDB) without requiring an Internet Gateway or NAT Gateway?
questions.why: VPC Endpoints (Gateway or Interface endpoints) enable private connectivity between your VPC and supported AWS services, keeping traffic entirely within the AWS network.

questions.text: A developer wants to safely store application secrets like database passwords and third-party API keys, and have them rotated automatically. Which service is best?
questions.why: AWS Secrets Manager helps you protect secrets needed to access your applications, services, and IT resources, and natively supports automatic password rotation for databases.

questions.text: Which migration strategy involves modifying the application architecture to take full advantage of cloud-native features, such as moving from a monolithic application to serverless microservices?
questions.why: Refactoring (or Rearchitecting) involves completely reimagining how the application is architected and developed using cloud-native features (like Lambda, DynamoDB) to improve agility, performance, or scalability.

questions.text: To optimize costs, a company wants to find idle or underutilized EC2 instances and receive recommendations to downsize them. Which AWS service provides this functionality?
questions.why: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze historical utilization metrics and recommend optimal AWS compute resources to reduce costs and improve performance.

questions.text: Which AWS feature acts as a stateful firewall for Amazon EC2 instances, allowing you to control inbound and outbound traffic?
questions.why: Security Groups act as a virtual, stateful firewall for your EC2 instances to control incoming and outgoing traffic. (NACLs act at the subnet level and are stateless).

questions.text: A data engineering team wants an interactive, serverless query service to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Which service fits this need?
questions.why: Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. It is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to manage.

questions.text: Which fully managed continuous integration (CI) service compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy?
questions.why: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy.

questions.text: Which cloud computing characteristic states that you only pay for the individual resources you consume, and only for as long as you consume them?
questions.why: Pay-as-you-go is a fundamental pricing model of cloud computing where you trade capital expense for variable expense and only pay for what you use.

questions.text: A developer needs to establish a dedicated hardware security module (HSM) in the AWS Cloud to meet corporate compliance requirements for key management. Which service should they use?
questions.why: AWS CloudHSM provides hardware security modules in the AWS Cloud. It allows you to easily generate and use your own encryption keys in a single-tenant hardware appliance.

questions.text: Which AWS service is designed to help developers extract text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents using machine learning?
questions.why: Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts printed text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents, going beyond simple OCR.

questions.text: You need a fast and flexible NoSQL database service for a high-traffic mobile app that requires single-digit millisecond latency. Which service is appropriate?
questions.why: Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.

questions.text: Which service acts as a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications?
questions.why: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service used to decouple applications, ensuring messages are stored safely until processed.

questions.text: A company requires 100% control over the operating system of the database server and needs to install custom database software. Which AWS solution provides this level of control?

options.text: Database running on an Amazon EC2 instance

questions.why: Running a database directly on an EC2 instance gives you full administrative root access to the operating system, allowing you to install any custom software you need. RDS does not provide OS access.

questions.text: Under the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar focuses on the ability to support development and run workloads effectively, gain insight into their operations, and continuously improve supporting processes?
questions.why: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value, and continually improving processes and procedures (like Infrastructure as Code and automated deployments).

questions.text: Which AWS service tracks API calls made within your AWS account and helps with auditing and governance by answering 'Who did what, and when?'
questions.why: AWS CloudTrail records AWS API calls for your account, providing a history of actions taken via the AWS Management Console, SDKs, command line tools, and other AWS services.

questions.text: A startup is working on a tight budget and wants to set custom spending limits and receive email alerts if their AWS costs exceed these limits. Which tool should they use?
questions.why: AWS Budgets gives you the ability to set custom budgets that alert you when your costs or usage exceed (or are forecasted to exceed) your budgeted amount.

questions.text: Which service acts as a highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service designed to route end users to internet applications?
questions.why: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud DNS web service used for domain registration, DNS routing, and health checking.

questions.text: If a company wants to provide its remote employees with a secure, managed, cloud-based virtual desktop environment, which service should they use?
questions.why: Amazon WorkSpaces is a fully managed, secure Desktop-as-a-Service (DaaS) solution that helps you provision Windows or Linux desktops for your remote workers in minutes.

questions.text: Which AWS networking component allows instances in a private subnet to securely access the public Internet for software updates while preventing inbound traffic?
questions.why: A NAT (Network Address Translation) Gateway, placed in a public subnet, allows instances in a private subnet to connect to the internet while stopping the internet from establishing connections back to the instances.

questions.text: A developer wants to provision a secure private connection between an on-premises facility and an AWS VPC that bypasses the public internet completely. Which service is required?
questions.why: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated private physical network connection from your premises to AWS, which bypassing the public internet, offering lower latency and higher security.

questions.text: Which AWS service makes it easy to set up and manage a scalable data lake securely in days instead of months?
questions.why: AWS Lake Formation is a fully managed service that simplifies and automates the complex manual steps required to create, manage, and secure a data lake.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: Which global infrastructure concept is described as one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity in an AWS Region?
questions.why: An Availability Zone (AZ) consists of one or more discrete, physical data centers, each with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, housed in separate facilities within a Region.

questions.text: Which service simplifies discovering, cataloging, cleaning, and transforming data across your enterprise to prepare it for analytics and machine learning?
questions.why: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that makes it easy for customers to prepare and load their data for analytics.

questions.text: A company wants to manage and deploy SSL/TLS certificates for their Application Load Balancers and CloudFront distributions automatically. Which service handles this?
questions.why: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is a service that lets you easily provision, manage, and deploy public and private Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates for use with AWS services.

questions.text: According to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF), which perspective focuses on ensuring that IT aligns with business needs and that IT investments map to key business results?
questions.why: The Business perspective helps stakeholders understand how to update the staff skills and organizational processes they will need to optimize business value as they move to the cloud.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used to centrally manage single sign-on (SSO) access to multiple AWS accounts and business applications like Office 365 or Salesforce?
questions.why: AWS IAM Identity Center (the successor to AWS Single Sign-On) is the recommended service for centrally managing human user access across multiple AWS accounts and cloud applications.

questions.text: A company wants a comprehensive, itemized view of their AWS billing data, updated multiple times a day, which can be delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket for analysis. What should they use?
questions.why: The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) contains the most comprehensive set of AWS cost and usage data available, delivered to an S3 bucket in CSV or Parquet format.

questions.text: Which AWS service is designed to automate the setup of a multi-account AWS environment (landing zone) using best practices for security and governance?
questions.why: AWS Control Tower provides the easiest way to set up and govern a secure, multi-account AWS environment (called a landing zone) based on AWS best practices.

questions.text: A developer needs a managed service to run Kubernetes workloads on AWS without having to install and operate the Kubernetes control plane. Which service should they use?
questions.why: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) is a managed service that makes it easy to run Kubernetes on AWS without needing to install, operate, and maintain your own Kubernetes control plane.

questions.text: A media company wants to speed up content uploads from global users to a centralized Amazon S3 bucket. Which S3 feature routes traffic through the AWS edge network to accelerate this process?
questions.why: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration enables fast, easy, and secure transfers of files over long distances between a client and an S3 bucket by utilizing Amazon CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations.

questions.text: Which service brings AWS infrastructure and services closer to the edge of the 5G network to provide ultra-low latency for mobile applications?
questions.why: AWS Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage services within telecommunications providers' datacenters at the edge of the 5G network for ultra-low latency mobile apps.

questions.text: Which AWS service allows you to centrally manage and automate data protection (backups) across AWS services such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, and EFS?
questions.why: AWS Backup is a fully managed, policy-based service that makes it easy to centralize and automate the back up of data across AWS services in the cloud as well as on-premises.

questions.text: A financial firm requires compliance with a mandate to ensure their data written to Amazon S3 cannot be deleted or overwritten for a specific period of time (WORM model). What feature should they use?
questions.why: Amazon S3 Object Lock enables you to store objects using a write-once-read-many (WORM) model, preventing them from being deleted or overwritten for a fixed amount of time or indefinitely.

questions.text: Which AWS migration service is used to gather information about your on-premises servers, including their usage and configuration, to help plan your migration to AWS?
questions.why: AWS Application Discovery Service helps enterprise customers plan migration projects by gathering information about their on-premises data centers, server utilization data, and dependency mappings.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of Amazon API Gateway?

options.text: To route network traffic to the closest AWS Region
To create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale
To monitor and alert on API usage billing costs
To translate speech into text through APIs

questions.why: Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs (REST, HTTP, WebSocket) at any scale.

questions.text: Which AWS service is specifically designed to provide automated, continuous threat detection for Amazon S3 by using machine learning to discover and protect sensitive data like PII?
questions.why: Amazon Macie is a data security service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data (such as Personally Identifiable Information) in AWS.

questions.text: A developer wants to implement a fully managed Business Intelligence (BI) tool to create interactive dashboards and visualize data. Which service should they choose?
questions.why: Amazon QuickSight is a scalable, serverless, embeddable, machine learning-powered business intelligence (BI) service built for the cloud to create interactive dashboards.

questions.text: Which AWS storage service provides a high-performance file system optimized for fast processing of compute-intensive workloads, such as High-Performance Computing (HPC) and machine learning?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.why: Amazon FSx for Lustre provides a high-performance file system optimized for fast processing of workloads such as machine learning, high performance computing (HPC), video processing, and financial modeling.

questions.text: Which tool provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions?
questions.why: AWS Migration Hub provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions, giving you visibility into the status of your portfolio.

questions.text: A company wants to introduce chaos engineering into their architecture to test how their applications withstand unexpected disruptions. Which service facilitates this?
questions.why: AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS), formerly Fault Injection Simulator, is a fully managed service for running fault injection experiments (chaos engineering) to improve application performance, observability, and resiliency.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: What is the most cost-effective S3 storage class for data with unknown or changing access patterns?
questions.why: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves data to the most cost-effective access tier based on access frequency, without performance impact or operational overhead, saving costs when access patterns change.

questions.text: Which AWS service is a managed, serverless GraphQL API service that simplifies application development by letting developers create a flexible API to securely access, manipulate, and combine data from one or more data sources?
questions.why: AWS AppSync is a fully managed service that makes it easy to develop GraphQL APIs by handling the heavy lifting of securely connecting to data sources like DynamoDB, Lambda, and more.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: A company has petabytes of on-premises data and needs to migrate it to AWS over an active internet connection. Which online data transfer service simplifies and accelerates moving data between on-premises storage and AWS?
questions.why: AWS DataSync is a secure, online service that automates and accelerates moving data between on-premises storage (like NFS/SMB) and AWS storage services (like S3, EFS, FSx).
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: Which service gives you a comprehensive view of your security state in AWS and helps you check your environment against security industry standards and best practices?
questions.why: AWS Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security alerts and security posture across your AWS accounts, automatically aggregating findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, etc.

questions.text: A retail company wants to use machine learning to build an application that can forecast inventory demand based on historical time-series data. Which AWS service provides this functionality?
questions.why: Amazon Forecast is a time-series forecasting service based on machine learning. It is built for business metrics forecasting like inventory demand, financial planning, and resource allocation.
questions.priorityNote: closed to new customers, not on the in-scope list

questions.text: Which of the following is a managed service that makes it easy to build, train, and deploy machine learning models quickly?
questions.why: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed platform that enables developers and data scientists to quickly and easily build, train, and deploy machine learning models at any scale.

questions.text: Which AWS networking feature allows you to securely expose a service in your VPC to another AWS account's VPC without requiring an Internet Gateway or VPC Peering?
questions.why: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs, AWS services, and on-premises applications, securely on the Amazon network, without exposing traffic to the public internet.

questions.text: A company wants to minimize the recovery time objective (RTO) in the event of a disaster for their critical on-premises servers. Which AWS service continuously replicates servers to AWS to ensure fast recovery?
questions.why: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) minimizes downtime and data loss with fast, reliable recovery of on-premises and cloud-based applications using affordable storage, minimal compute, and point-in-time recovery.

questions.text: Which service acts as a repository for discovering, deploying, and publishing serverless applications?
questions.why: The AWS Serverless Application Repository is a managed repository for serverless applications, enabling teams to securely store and share reusable applications, and easily assemble and deploy serverless architectures.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: A developer needs a native Windows file system for an application built on .NET that is migrating to AWS. Which storage service should they use?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.why: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed, highly reliable, and scalable file storage that is accessible over the industry-standard SMB protocol, designed specifically for Windows workloads.
questions.concept: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.text: Which AWS pricing tool helps you build a business case by analyzing your on-premises infrastructure and providing an estimated cost comparison for running the same workloads on AWS?
questions.why: Migration Evaluator (formerly TCO Calculator) helps build a data-driven business case for migrating to AWS by analyzing your existing on-premises inventory and projecting AWS costs.

questions.text: In Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, what defines the maximum number of instances that the group can scale out to?
questions.why: The Auto Scaling Group's size is constrained by the Minimum Capacity and Maximum Capacity. The Maximum Capacity dictates the absolute upper limit of instances that can be launched.

questions.text: Which AWS Support Plan provides a concierge-like billing and account support function for billing and account inquiries?
questions.why: The Enterprise Support plan provides access to an AWS Support Concierge, a senior customer service agent assigned to your account who assists with billing and account-level inquiries.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fully managed search and analytics engine used for log analytics, real-time application monitoring, and clickstream analysis?
questions.why: Amazon OpenSearch Service (successor to Amazon Elasticsearch Service) makes it easy to perform interactive log analytics, real-time application monitoring, and website search.

questions.text: A developer needs to store unstructured configuration files and standard passwords. Which free service provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management?
questions.why: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and secrets management (like passwords). It is free for standard parameters, unlike Secrets Manager which charges per secret.

questions.text: Which service automatically continuously monitors your AWS environment to simplify risk and compliance assessment against frameworks like GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI?
questions.why: AWS Audit Manager helps you continuously audit your AWS usage to simplify how you assess risk and compliance with regulations and industry standards by automatically collecting evidence.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: A company wants to stream non-persistent applications to their users' web browsers without rewriting the applications for the web. Which service allows application streaming?
questions.why: Amazon AppStream 2.0 is a fully managed non-persistent application and desktop streaming service. It centrally manages desktop applications and securely delivers them to any computer.

questions.text: Which fully managed continuous deployment service automates software deployments to compute services such as Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda, and your on-premises servers?
questions.why: AWS CodeDeploy is a deployment service that automates application deployments to various compute services, minimizing downtime during application updates.
questions.priorityNote: not on the CLF-C02 in-scope list

questions.text: A small business needs to quickly deploy a simple web application using a predefined tech stack (like LAMP or Node.js) with predictable pricing. Which service is designed for this simplicity?
questions.why: Amazon Lightsail is an easy-to-use virtual private server (VPS) that offers you everything needed to build an application or website, plus a cost-effective, monthly plan.

questions.text: Which cloud computing deployment model allows a company to run applications in an environment that meets strict government regulations while utilizing shared cloud benefits, but strictly isolated from the general public?
questions.why: AWS GovCloud (US) is an isolated set of AWS Regions for US government agencies and regulated customers, operated by screened US citizens and built for requirements like FedRAMP High and ITAR. It's still AWS cloud infrastructure rather than a private cloud you own, but it's isolated from the standard Regions, which makes it the best fit among these choices.

questions.text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar includes the design principle of 'Stop guessing your capacity needs'?
questions.why: Stopping guessing capacity is a design principle of the Reliability pillar (as well as Cost Optimization in some contexts). By using cloud elasticity, you eliminate the risk of failure due to under-provisioning or paying for over-provisioning.

questions.text: What does Amazon EBS use to create point-in-time, incremental copies of your data to save in Amazon S3 for backup purposes?
questions.why: EBS Snapshots are point-in-time, incremental backups of EBS volumes that are stored in Amazon S3, allowing you to recreate the volume if needed.

questions.text: A developer is writing code that must continuously poll a message queue and process the contents. If there are no messages, the system spins and wastes CPU cycles. Which Amazon SQS feature resolves this by waiting for messages to arrive?
questions.why: Long Polling reduces the number of empty responses by allowing SQS to wait until a message is available in the queue before sending a response, thus saving CPU cycles and API costs.

questions.text: Which service enables developers to build full-stack web and mobile applications quickly, complete with authentication, storage, and API hosting?
questions.why: AWS Amplify is a set of tools and services that can be used together or on their own, to help front-end web and mobile developers build scalable full stack applications powered by AWS.
